name: PostgreSQL Migration Assessment
description: Captures PostgreSQL-specific target, compatibility, migration, validation and operating decisions that complement automated discovery.

sections.title: PostgreSQL Workload & Target
sections.description: Identify scope, workload ownership, release constraints and the intended target.

questions.text: Which databases and schemas are in scope for this migration?
What are the primary workload patterns?
Are application deployments tightly coupled to database schema migrations?
Describe peak periods, maintenance windows and long-running batch processes.
Which PostgreSQL migration destination and target major version are being evaluated?
options: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

sections.title: Extensions & Compatibility
sections.description: Decide how discovered extensions, privileged capabilities and PostgreSQL semantics will be handled.

questions.text: Which discovered extensions are business-critical, removable or require replacement on the target?
questions.helpText: Identify each required extension, its business purpose, target support status and remediation owner.

questions.text: Does application code require superuser privileges or direct access to the server file system?
Are foreign data wrappers used in critical data paths?
Describe dependencies on logical decoding, custom C extensions, procedural languages, large objects or unlogged tables.
Does application behavior depend on source locale, collation, encoding or time-zone semantics?
Are PgBouncer, another connection pooler or connection-routing proxies required?
Describe large-table partitioning, sequence synchronization or large-object constraints that affect migration.

sections.title: Migration & High Availability
sections.description: Define data movement, compatibility, cutover and continuity expectations.

questions.text: What migration method is preferred for this PostgreSQL workload?
Must existing replication slots or downstream logical subscribers be preserved?
What target high-availability model is required?
Have source-to-target version, extension, collation, encoding and feature compatibility prerequisites been verified?
Has secure connectivity and sustained migration throughput been tested with production-scale data?
Can source schema and application changes be frozen during final migration and validation?
Describe the rollback method and rollback decision triggers.

sections.title: Validation & Cutover Readiness
sections.description: Define acceptance evidence, performance thresholds, rehearsals and approvals.

questions.text: Which source-to-target validation checks are required for acceptance?
Who owns data reconciliation and can accept documented variances?
Have peak-load baselines and target performance acceptance thresholds been agreed?
options: Baselines captured but thresholds not agreed

questions.text: What is the status of the production-scale migration rehearsal?
Who provides final business, application, database, security and operations sign-off?

sections.title: Security & Operations
sections.description: Capture authentication, configuration and post-migration ownership requirements.

questions.text: Which authentication methods must be supported on the target?
Which custom pg_hba.conf, postgresql.conf or operating-system settings are mandatory, and what is their target disposition?
Describe current backup, point-in-time recovery, vacuum and statistics maintenance processes.
Who will own extension upgrades, query tuning, monitoring and incident response after migration?
